properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the block that "matched command TEXT, not intent" came from hxm_program's OWN PreToolUse hook, which matches the whole Bash command text on purpose and documents that false positive; reflow2 ships no such hook. reflow2's part is that a DesignRule can say only WHETHER it stops things (enforced) and nothing about WHAT ACTION it guards or where it is enforced, so a conduct rule's scope and its known false positives live only in a project script's comments
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-28, reflow2 0.73.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. Item F-35.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "An enforced rule matched command TEXT, not intent, and blocked local work twice. `rule:no-remote-host-access-by-agent` (a rule I would not weaken) refused: a local `grep` whose path list named two access-restricted repo directories; a local file edit whose *content* contained remote-desktop and secure-copy command examples written *for AJ to run*. Neither opened a session anywhere. The workaround (move the text through the editor tool) cost a retry each time and teaches the agent to route around the guard, which is the wrong lesson." EXPECTED: local reads and file writes pass; only an action that opens a session on a remote host is refused. NOT AFFECTED: the same text written through the editor tool went through, and real remote commands are refused as intended.

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): nothing on a rule matching command text. The same hub's 2026-09-14 /feedback entry already saw it once: "This repo's PreToolUse hook blocks shell commands that look like remote host access. It fired on a command whose only offence was the word 'ssh' inside prose... The guard is right and I would not weaken it, but the recovery path cost two retries" (in the same file, uncaptured until now). rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground: reflow2 targets any MCP client and rides no harness hook except the optional loop-nudge adapters. The same hub's 2026-09-08 entry asked for a target a conduct rule could be GOVERNED_BY ("a DesignRule about agent conduct has no Component"), also never recorded.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) THE PROJECT'S OWN ENFORCEMENT: hxm_program's harness hook matches command text.
(B) reflow2 SHIPS OR INSTALLS a hook that checks enforced DesignRules against tool calls.
(C) HARNESS CONTRACT: a Bash-side hook is handed only the command string, so any guard there is a text parser.
(D) reflow2 GOVERNANCE VOCABULARY: an enforced DesignRule records only that it is gate-blocking and owes a detector; it cannot say what action it guards or where it is enforced, so the project had to write a word list, and nothing in the design shows the matcher's scope.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: the grep block was the rule working (reading the restricted checkouts is inside the rule), or the block came from a permissions deny rule rather than the hook.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: A predicts a project hook whose matcher is textual; B predicts a reflow2 file installing a PreToolUse hook; C predicts the hook's input is {tool_input:{command}} only; D predicts DesignRule declares no property for an action or an enforcement point; E predicts the refused grep reads inside the restricted checkouts, or a deny rule matching it.

⑤ RESULTS:
· hxm_program's .claude/settings.json (checkout 77d2f1f, 2026-09-23, read-only) wires PreToolUse matcher Bash to tools/hooks/no-remote-shell.sh, statusMessage naming the rule, plus three permissions deny rules on Read of the restricted checkouts. The script's own header: "Known false positive, accepted on purpose: the match is on the whole command TEXT, so prose in a heredoc (a commit message saying "the agent ssh'd in", "the ansible role") trips it. Put such prose in a file with the Write tool and pass the file ... Strict beats clever." ⇒ A HOLDS. The editor-tool route the reporter calls routing around the guard is the route the hook's author prescribed for prose.
· reflow2 repo (crates, skills, getting-started, tools): no file mentions PreToolUse; reflow2's shipped hooks are SessionStart and Stop (the loop nudge). ⇒ B REFUTED.
· The hook run on 8 synthetic commands in a scratch folder: REFUSED: a grep naming the restricted checkouts as search roots; an rg EXCLUDING them by full path; a heredoc file write holding ssh/scp examples; `echo "ask AJ to run: ssh somehost" >> notes.md`; `git commit -m "the ansible role needs a fix"`; a real ssh. ALLOWED: a grep excluding them by bare directory name; a remote-desktop client command, which is not in the word list. So the matcher over-blocks prose and exclusions and under-blocks at least one way of opening a session on a remote host. ⇒ C HOLDS as a constraint: the hook reads `.tool_input.command` and nothing else.
· schema/core.yaml DesignRule declares name, statement, category, steps, units, enforced. `enforced` means "violations are gate-blocking (and owes a detector)". `steps` names only SERVED skills and tools and is validated against them, so it cannot name a harness action such as a shell command. The governance-proposal skill says enforced:true means "stop the build" and asks for a passing Verification; a conduct rule's enforcement point, the agent's own tool call, is outside reflow2's reach by rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground. ⇒ D HOLDS.
· E: whether the refused grep read inside the checkouts or only named them to exclude is NOT ESTABLISHED; the report does not give the command. If it searched them, that block was the rule working (the restricted-path clause was added 2026-09-08 after an agent read one). The file-edit block is a false positive by the hook's own account.

⑥ CLASS: a safety rule enforced by a text matcher at a boundary that sees only text, where the accepted false positives, and any false negatives, are recorded only in the script's comments. For reflow2 the class is D: the rule vocabulary records WHETHER a rule stops things, never WHAT it guards or WHERE, so the passing check attached to the rule proves it catches violations and says nothing about what else it blocks or misses. The governance-proposal skill warns that a passing check can green-wash an under-detecting rule; the over-blocking direction has no home at all. Would a fix at D have prevented today's blocks? Not the text matching, since the harness still hands text. It would have put the rule's scope and its known false positives in the design, where an agent reads the rule before acting, so the prose could have gone through the editor tool the first time; the 09-14 sighting says the same retry recurred.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code was changed. A class-pinning test for reflow2 would assert that a DesignRule can carry what it guards (an action kind and target) and its check's recorded exclusions, and that the governance-proposal skill asks for both when a rule is enforced outside the build. For hxm_program, a table test of the hook over true positives and true negatives (the eight commands above) would pin its own scope; that is the project's to take.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. HELD: the refusal matched command text, not intent; the file edit opened no session. QUALIFIED: "an enforced rule" did the matching. It was hxm_program's own hook, not anything reflow2 enforces. "Neither opened a session" holds for the edit and is not established for the grep. "Teaches the agent to route around the guard": the editor-tool path is the one the hook's author wrote down for prose, so it is compliance, though nothing in the design tells an agent that before the retry. NEW: the word list misses at least one remote-session tool, a false negative for the owner to judge.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the exact refused commands; whether the reporting machine's hook matches the 2026-09-23 checkout read here (its last change is e7182b8, 2026-09-08); whether the file edit ran through Bash or another tool the hook does not match; the permissions deny rules' reach over Grep was not exercised.
